D.t: Lynne Walz trails by 4.5 and wins 19% of simulations. Closing it takes about 17,441 voters switching sides, or 34,881 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +11.1 and D +2.1. A normal polling error decides it.

The polls page average is R +5.0. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners for Education Reform Now Advocacy (D) at D +0.3; your worst is Echelon Insights for NetChoice at R +7.3. 9 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Douglas, a projected net 59,939 votes; Lancaster, a projected net 33,224 votes; Sarpy, a projected net 6,347 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sarpy, D +8.2, 10.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Lynne Walz runs furthest behind in Platte, Madison, Washington. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 42 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.50 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 70% of voters, 44 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.49 points; Voters without a degree, 59% of voters, 41 to 53, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.97 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Lynne Walz: Immigration voters 16 to 78, Small counties 27 to 67, Voters who can afford daily costs 41 to 53. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$860K cash against $7.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points toward Lynne Walz. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
